bar-counter.definition: A long counter where drinks and other items are prepared, displayed, or served in a bar setting.
bar-counter.exampleUsage: The interior-design plan places stools along the bar counter.

bar-stool.definition: A tall seat designed for use at a high counter.
bar-stool.exampleUsage: The bar stool has a footrest beneath the seat.

back-bar.definition: The shelves, cabinets, and display area behind a bar counter.
back-bar.exampleUsage: The back bar contained labeled glassware and display bottles.

draft-taps.definition: Taps connected to a pressurized beverage system for dispensing drinks from containers or lines.
draft-taps.exampleUsage: The venue diagram labels the draft taps behind the counter.

bottle-display.definition: An arranged group of bottles shown on shelves or in a cabinet.
bottle-display.exampleUsage: The bottle display was lit from behind.

ice-well.definition: An insulated container built into a service counter for holding ice.
ice-well.exampleUsage: The ice well was covered when not in use.

speed-rail.definition: A narrow rack attached near a service counter for holding frequently handled bottles or containers.
speed-rail.exampleUsage: The speed rail is mounted below the counter edge.

garnish-tray.definition: A compartmented tray used to hold decorative food items such as fruit pieces or herbs.
garnish-tray.exampleUsage: The garnish tray had separate covered sections.

bar-mat.definition: A rubber or plastic mat placed on a counter to catch drips and provide a non-slip surface.
bar-mat.exampleUsage: The bar mat protected the counter from spills.

lounge-area.definition: An area in a building set aside for sitting and relaxing.

cocktail-glass.definition: A stemmed glass with a wide bowl, traditionally associated with mixed drinks.
cocktail-glass.exampleUsage: The display case included an empty cocktail glass.

highball-glass.definition: A tall drinking glass designed for serving mixed drinks, especially those combined with a larger amount of soda or other mixer.

rocks-glass.definition: A short, wide drinking glass with a thick base.
rocks-glass.exampleUsage: The glassware exhibit included a rocks glass.

shot-glass.definition: A small glass used to serve a small measure of a drink.

wine-glass.definition: A drinking glass with a bowl, stem, and base, traditionally used for wine.
wine-glass.exampleUsage: The table-setting display included an empty wine glass.

champagne-flute.definition: A slender stemmed glass with a tall narrow bowl.
champagne-flute.exampleUsage: The empty Champagne flute has a tall narrow bowl.

beer-mug.definition: A mug designed to hold and serve beer.
beer-mug.exampleUsage: The display places the beer mug beside the other empty glasses.

collins-glass.definition: A tall, narrow drinking glass with straight sides.
collins-glass.exampleUsage: The glassware chart shows the shape of a Collins glass.

coupe-glass.definition: A stemmed glass with a broad, shallow bowl.
coupe-glass.exampleUsage: The display included a coupe glass with a shallow bowl.

snifter.definition: A globular glass with a small top.

cocktail-shaker.definition: A container with a tight lid used to combine cocktail ingredients by shaking.
cocktail-shaker.exampleUsage: The equipment list includes a cocktail shaker and a measuring jigger.

jigger.definition: A small measuring tool used to measure beverage ingredients.

muddler.definition: A short bar tool used to press ingredients in a glass or mixing vessel.

bar-spoon.definition: A long-handled spoon used behind a service counter for stirring and handling ingredients.
bar-spoon.exampleUsage: The equipment display included a long bar spoon.

strainer.definition: A filter to retain larger pieces while smaller pieces and liquids pass through.

ice-tongs.definition: A gripping tool used to lift individual pieces of ice.
ice-tongs.exampleUsage: The ice tongs grip individual ice cubes.

bottle-opener.definition: A handheld tool designed to pry caps or pull corks from bottles.
bottle-opener.exampleUsage: The attendant puts the bottle opener in the tool drawer.

citrus-press.definition: A hand tool or device used to squeeze juice from citrus fruit.
citrus-press.exampleUsage: The citrus press extracts juice from lemons and limes.

zester.definition: A small kitchen tool used to remove thin strips of the colored outer peel of citrus fruit.
zester.exampleUsage: The zester removed a thin strip of lemon peel.

bartender.definition: A worker who prepares and serves drinks at a bar.

barback.definition: A worker who supports bartending staff by stocking, cleaning, and organizing the service area.
barback.exampleUsage: The barback restocked clean glassware before the event.

mixologist.definition: A person who specializes in developing or preparing mixed drinks.

bouncer.definition: A security worker who helps manage entry and order at a venue.

host.definition: A staff member who welcomes guests and helps arrange seating or reservations.

cocktail-waitress.definition: A server in some bars or entertainment venues who brings drinks and other orders to customers.
cocktail-waitress.exampleUsage: The job-description example identifies a cocktail waitress as a venue server.

manager.definition: A person who controls resources and expenditures.

sommelier.definition: A specialist in wine selection and service, often in a restaurant.

dj.definition: A person who announces and plays popular recorded music.

promoter.definition: A person who advertises or organizes events to attract customers.

corkscrew.definition: A tool with a spiral metal point used to remove a cork from a bottle.
